clue.text: Build up a sound team of workers

indicators.note: a sound of something is how it comes across when spoken, so the phrase that follows is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a crew is a team of workers, as on a ship, with the article said along with it

explanation.surface: An employer is assembling a solid workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' sits in the middle of the wordplay and looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it is the signal that the team of workers is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest or debts accrue when they gradually pile up over time, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Bill leaves 1, uncertain of successful treatment

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so the short word for a bill departs from the earlier answer
letters that are uncertain are unsettled, so what remains is put into a fresh order

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A patient frets over whether the bill is still piling up after a treatment that may or may not have worked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AC from ACCRUE to leave CRUE, then rearrange it into CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that works restores health, which is exactly what a medical cure is.

clue.text: Slump in the intermission, with no one rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the words are read from the bottom upwards, so their order is turned round

blocks.note: a recess is a break or interval

explanation.surface: Audience numbers drop off during the interval, with nobody getting up from their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one' reads as nobody, but here it is two separate words, a refusal and the Roman numeral, and both are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slump is a period of falling activity, which economists call a recession.

clue.text: Weather to continue?

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to come through a storm or hardship
second meaning: to last or go on existing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the current spell of weather will last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weather' looks like a noun about the forecast; it is the verb, as in weathering a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather hardship is to bear it, and things that last a long time are said to persist; one verb covers both.

clue.text: Bag studio communication system

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptically: the word bag is gab written backwards, and gab means talk
second meaning: the intercom linking a control room with presenters or performers

explanation.surface: A bag of kit for a studio's intercom set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Bag' as GAB in reverse: gab is talk, so bag is talk, back. That whimsical reading gives the phrase TALK BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: In broadcasting, the talkback is the intercom line through which producers speak to presenters and crew during a programme.

clue.text: The strain of church union

blocks.note: surface reading: the stress put on a church's members or a merger of denominations
setter's reading: a strain is a tune, and a church union is a marriage, so this is the music played as a bride processes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests tension; here it means a piece of music, and the union is a wedding held in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Mendelssohn or Wagner piece played at weddings is the tune for a couple being joined in church.

clue.text: Research centre has model cloned finally and tagged

indicators.note: finally points to the end of a word, so only its closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: A laboratory has copied a model organism and attached identifying tags to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a scientific prototype in the lab scene, but it is Elle, the supermodel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tagged has been given a label identifying it, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Begin differently, in essence

indicators.note: doing something differently means arranging it another way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to start afresh with a fundamentally new approach.
explanation.definitionFit: One's being is one's fundamental nature or existence, the core quality otherwise called one's essence.

clue.text: Sudden, painful withdrawal from unfriendly country

blocks.note: the nation spanning Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: An army makes an abrupt, costly retreat from hostile territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a military pull-out; the withdrawal is from a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting an addictive drug abruptly, with harsh symptoms rather than tapering off, is known by this slang phrase.

clue.text: Heath cut by unemployed comic writer

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, so it loses its final letter

blocks.note: erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: A man called Heath is laid off by a comedy writer with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: ERICA loses its last letter to give ERIC. Eric Idle is a member of the Monty Python comedy team, and wrote much of its material.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monty Python performer is well known for writing comedy songs, sketches and the musical Spamalot.

clue.text: Restrain brother as above?

blocks.note: the second word of 9 across, the entry directly above, meaning unemployed

explanation.surface: Someone tells a sibling to hold back, just as instructed previously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as above' points to 9 across, whose second word is IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle a horse or one's temper is to hold it in check, so the verb means to curb.

clue.text: They show the way trees changed, though at first a slight change

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so those letters are rearranged
at first points to the beginning of a word, so only its opening letter is used
a change applied to the word before it means its letters are reordered too

explanation.surface: Guides note that the trees along a route have altered, if only a little at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue holds two separate rearrangement signals, each working only on the word just before it, with a single initial letter between the two results.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps along a road illuminate the route for travellers at night, so they show people where to go.

clue.text: Risky, like tip-and-run

blocks.note: to tip something is to touch it lightly

explanation.surface: Tip-and-run is a form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the bat touches the ball; it is called a hazardous game.
explanation.walkthrough: Each part of the hyphenated game name is replaced by a synonym, in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch-and-go situation is precarious, with the outcome uncertain, so it is hazardous or chancy.

clue.text: Look at more than a hundred places

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
in Roman numerals CI is 101, one more than a hundred

explanation.surface: An invitation to examine over a hundred locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than a hundred' sounds vague but is the precise Roman numeral for 101.
explanation.definitionFit: Loci is the Latin plural of locus, a position or site, used in maths, genetics and law.

clue.text: Idealists, poor dears, getting me right in

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the word beside it is broken up and rearranged
getting something in means taking it inside, so those letters go into the rearranged word

explanation.surface: Someone pities a group of starry-eyed folk and lets the speaker into their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The additions go inside the rearranged word just before its final letter; R for right is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue visions that may never come true, and such impractical visionaries are said to have their heads in the clouds.

clue.text: Spirit abroad at night?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the light of the moon, out and about after dark

blocks.note: second meaning: the moon's light, which is out and about only after dark

explanation.surface: A ghost wandering about after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost and 'abroad' means out and about, not overseas; the question mark flags the playful second meaning, moonlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg whisky is called by this name, and the same word means the light given off by the moon.

clue.text: Top student is in a small boat

indicators.note: one thing that is in another sits inside it, so the letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a pinnace is a ship's small tender

explanation.surface: A top-performing student is out sailing in a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the learner sign displayed by British learner drivers, goes inside PINNACE before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a mountain or of achievement is its peak, which is the noun's meaning.

clue.text: Analysis of metrical patterns locates containers in Israel

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so the following word wraps those letters

blocks.note: Sion, or Zion, is a poetic name for Israel

explanation.surface: A literary study turns up storage jars at a site in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanning a line of verse means marking its stressed and unstressed syllables, and the noun for that study is this.

clue.text: One mobile holds ten beasts

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the word before it shift into a new order
a word that holds something has it inside, so the numeral goes within

explanation.surface: A single mobile phone contains ten animals, perhaps as photos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone; it signals that ONE is rearranged to OEN, around X.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught cattle used for ploughing are animals, so the plural noun is an example of beasts.

clue.text: Noise heard from sailing ship

indicators.note: heard means taken in by the ear, so the word for the noise is spelt differently but said the same

blocks.note: a bark is a dog's noise

explanation.surface: Sounds carry across the water from a passing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a three-masted vessel with sails, square-rigged on all but the aftermost mast.

clue.text: Balances, they say, and averages resources

indicators.note: what they say is what people utter, so the preceding word is represented by its spoken form

blocks.note: balances in the sense of weighs up

explanation.surface: An accountant's checklist: balances, averages and what funds there are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balances' looks like a noun in a financial report; here it is the verb, weighs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase denotes the money and methods available to achieve something, so it matches resources.

clue.text: Fellows coming up in a year for the church council?

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means travelling from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards
in places the year inside the other word

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: University fellows rise in rank within a year, perhaps to sit on the church's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: DONS read upwards gives SNOD, with Y placed after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and sometimes laity that governs a church.

clue.text: Report to outlaw force

blocks.note: to outlaw something is to prohibit it
g is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: Informing on someone so the police can bar them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like the verb to inform; it is the noun, the sound of a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: The report of a gun is the loud explosive noise it makes when fired.

clue.text: Having former PM in charge is like paradise

blocks.note: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957

explanation.surface: A political commentator says that having an ex-premier back running things would be heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise, so the adjective formed from it describes a blissful idyllic place.

clue.text: Leave without real satisfaction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the outer word goes around the other

explanation.surface: Someone resigns without having found genuine fulfilment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking; it is used in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Requital is repayment or compensation, the sense of satisfaction in which a wronged party is given redress.

clue.text: Hold gems ordered for metallic fabric

indicators.note: ordered means put into an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A jeweller orders a mesh setting to keep stones in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh woven from fine gold wire is a textile made of metal, used in jewellery and evening bags.

clue.text: Force us to leave Guernsey in confusion

indicators.note: letters that leave a word depart from it, so they are taken out
confusion means disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Islanders are forced out of Guernsey amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb in an evacuation; it is the noun. Take U and S from GUERNSEY and rearrange GERNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use energy is power or vigour, and physics links work done to the forces applied.
